sonnet.problem: Card 17 already asked the point that blessing and cursing from the same mouth should not be. This card's right answer, 'One source shouldn't produce opposites', makes the same point again. It also states what the spring, fig tree and grapevine pictures stand for, which the passage does not say outright.
sonnet.rule: Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The question asks the baker to recall James's exact description of the tongue. The wrong answers are invented phrasings, so the baker cannot reason out 'restless evil full of deadly poison' from the earlier cards. It works as a wording guess.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
